paper_sections.title: Habenula alterations in resting state functional connectivity among autistic individuals
Associations Between Habenula Connectivity and Autism Symptomatology
Associations Between Habenula Connectivity and Autism Symptomatology

description.value: This multisite study examined resting-state functional connectivity of bilateral habenula regions in autistic and neurotypical participants, including group differences, age-by-group variability, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

spans.text: The resulting z-transformed (Fisher r-to-z transformation) correlation maps were entered into group-level regression models with diagnosis (ASD, NT) as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site using AFNI’s 3dLMEr ( 46 , 47 ).
Lastly, a separate regression analysis was performed to examine associations between atypical habenula connectivity and phenotypic measures, including SM, SC, EF, and DLS.

design.value: Large-scale, multisite, observational resting-state functional connectivity study using ABIDE I and II data, with ASD-versus-NT group comparisons, age-by-group interaction analyses, and exploratory associations with phenotypic measures.

spans.text: Participants for the current study were selected from the large-scale, multisite ABIDE I and II datasets.

The resulting z-transformed (Fisher r-to-z transformation) correlation maps were entered into group-level regression models with diagnosis (ASD, NT) as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site using AFNI’s 3dLMEr ( 46 , 47 ).
Next, z-transformed participant-level correlation maps were analyzed using a linear effects model to probe for age-by-group interactions, controlling for sex and scanning site.
Participants for the current study were selected from the large-scale, multisite ABIDE I and II datasets.
Further information regarding the ABIDE data collection can be found at http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/abide_I.html .
